subject: HTTP/2 trailer mismatch causing streaming parser failures — urgent escalation
messages:
From: Priya Desai <priya@ingestai.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Feb 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: spikes in latency + failed streams since SDK 2.3.1

Hi Karthik,

Since we upgraded to the client SDK 2.3.1 this morning we are seeing a 10-20x increase in error rate for streaming responses and a corresponding latency spike. The error looks like a parse failure in the streaming consumer: "incomplete trailer: expected 2 bytes but got 0". We attached a short snippet from our logs (error_trace.log.txt).

This is impacting our ingestion pipeline (throughput down ~60%) and a short outage window at 10:45 PT. Can you escalate? We need either a short-term mitigation (fallback to non-streaming endpoint) or a quick patch.

Thanks,
Priya
Principal Integrations Engineer
IngestAI

Attachments: error_trace.log.txt
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya@ingestai.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Feb 2027 17:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: spikes in latency + failed streams since SDK 2.3.1

Hi Priya — thanks for the report and the logs. I'm escalating immediately to our runtime team and looping in Laura (runtime lead) and Neha (customer success) so we can triage.

Short term: you can hit the non-streaming /v1/outputs endpoint with the same model and we will prioritize capacity for your account while we investigate. I'll report back within 90 minutes with an initial timeline.

-Karthik
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, Priya Desai <priya@ingestai.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 13 Feb 2027 18:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: spikes in latency + failed streams since SDK 2.3.1

Priya,

We pulled the trace. Initial hypothesis: the SDK's HTTP/2 framing change in 2.3.1 added optional trailers for model-metadata, and a subset of our client streaming parser treats missing/empty trailers as a fatal parse error. The runtime still emits valid frames, but there is a race where an intermediary (our edge proxy) can strip zero-length trailers which confuses downstream parsers.

Action plan (short):
- Flip a routing flag to force non-chunked streaming for IngestAI while we push a compatibility shim.
- Provide a small client patch to tolerate empty/missing trailers (bugfix build).
- Prepare a rollback for 2.3.1 at the SDK repo if customer impact widens.

I'll attach a short mitigation runbook and steps to apply the temporary routing flag.

Laura
Lead, Runtime Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation-runbook.pdf
From: Priya Desai <priya@ingestai.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 08:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: spikes in latency + failed streams since SDK 2.3.1

Thanks Laura — we applied the temporary routing flag per your instructions and error rate dropped to baseline. Two follow-ups: 1) can we get the client patch this week? 2) we would like a short note for our security/compliance team describing the issue (no data exposure, behavioral change only).

Also copying in Todd (integration lead) to confirm throughput recovery.

—Priya
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: spikes in latency + failed streams since SDK 2.3.1

Provide ETA for both by EOD Mon. Also include suggested customer accommodation (credits or extended support window) in your reply.

Rishi

Thanks for quick coordination and apologies for the disruption — we'll follow up with a short post-mortem and the release link.

Regards,
